Contents
Right-click the table above and choose Update Field if page numbers do not appear.
1. Purpose and Audience

This course takes an experienced SAP project manager who is new to security and GRC and prepares them to lead the security and GRC workstream of an SAP programme at an oil and gas company: to own the role model and the access governance tools, to direct security analysts, GRC administrators and Basis, to run access reviews and incidents, to bring identity and cloud access under control, and to defend the workstream to the steering committee and the auditors.

The participant plays Amara Osei, appointed GRC and Security Lead on the Corvane Energy Group controls project in week 9 (9 March 2026), working with Daniel Reyes, the Controls Lead. The case is the same company and project as the course From SAP Project Manager to Controls Lead; the security workstream is in the Corvane Security Extension Pack.

rows: SAP project and programme managers; delivery leads moving into a security, GRC or access governance lead role
Planning, budgeting, staffing, stakeholder and risk management; SAP landscape awareness; steering experience
SAP authorisation concepts; role design; GRC Access Control; identity and cloud access; access testing and audit expectations; incident handling for access faults

THE PRINCIPLE OF THE COURSE A security lead does not build every role or configure GRC. A security lead knows what a sound role model, rule set, access review and identity flow look like, can read SU53 and a GRC log well enough to challenge a diagnosis, and holds the line on access risk with the business and the auditor. The course teaches lead depth: enough to direct and challenge, not enough to replace the specialists.

Certification: an overall score of 75 percent, at least 70 percent on every element, a capstone total of 70 or more out of 100, and at least 21 of 30 on the capstone presentation. These are the same rules as the first course. Section 7 sets how marks become percentages.
7. Scoring Conversion Rules (Both Courses)

These rules apply to this course and to From SAP Project Manager to Controls Lead. They close the open item that the first course did not say how the Module 4 assessment and the practical became percentages.
7.1 General rules

rows: Element percentage.  Within an element, add the marks earned on the scored items and divide by the marks available, unless the element table in 7.2 gives each item a share. Multiply by 100.
Overall score.  Multiply each element percentage by its weight and add them.
Rounding.  Keep full precision for every threshold test (75, 70, 70 and 21). Report percentages to one decimal place. A score of 74.96 is not 75.
Missing work.  A scored item not submitted scores zero. With an agreed reason, the participant may submit it within two weeks of the due date without penalty.

Resubmission.  One resubmission is allowed per scored item that falls below 70 percent. The resubmitted mark is capped at 70 percent of the item. A capstone resubmission uses the second capstone case.
Two markers.  Where two markers score an item, the agreed mark stands. If they differ by more than 10 percent of the item's marks and cannot agree, a third marker decides.

Item pass marks inside a course.  An item may carry its own pass mark as a readiness signal (for example 80 for the Primer final assessment). Inside a course, certification uses only the element rules; an item below its own pass mark triggers a mentor conversation and a recommended retake, not a failure.

8. How to Run the Course
Cohort: 8 to 15 participants, one mentor per four. Mentors are current or former SAP security or GRC leads.
Rhythm: a weekly 90-minute live session for scenarios, war-room drills and case discussion; the rest is self-study.
Materials: the Corvane case file, the Corvane Security Extension Pack, Bridge Manual A, the Workbook Primer, Method Manual Part 3A and the new security manuals.
Environment: Excel and Word only. No SAP, GRC or cloud system access is needed; screens and outputs appear in the manuals and workbooks.

Entry: experience managing an SAP programme and the self-assessment in Appendix A. Participants who have finished the Controls Lead course may skip Module 1 and Module 8 and are credited with their Module 1 quiz mark.
Live drill: the week 8 session replays the 30 September war room (INC-09) with the participant in the chair.

1. Purpose and Decisions

This document fixes the scope of the second bridge course, From SAP Project Manager to GRC and Security Lead, before any course writing starts. The course uses the same company and the same project as the first course (From SAP Project Manager to Controls Lead): Corvane Energy Group and its 38-week SAP controls project. The participant is an experienced SAP project manager who moves into the GRC and Security Lead role on that project.

The scope was set by comparing the first-draft design with the TIB Security Lead programme (Modules 1 to 18 and the Senior/Lead add-on, Modules 19 to 24). Corvane already holds a complete access-control testing record, but the 24 modules also cover the work of building, running and fixing access. Those areas are added to Corvane as a new, fictitious Security and GRC Uplift workstream.

People are the existing Corvane cast plus the five new names in section 4; no other new names.
Verification for each workbook: all checks pass, zero formula errors, Ref_ tabs match their sources, and every FX fact quoted matches the data module.

Module 0 — Orientation and Self-Assessment

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Describe what a GRC and Security Lead does and decides. Place yourself in the Corvane security workstream. Agree a personal learning plan with your mentor.

blocks.text: 0.1 What the role is

A GRC and Security Lead owns how people get, keep and lose access to the SAP landscape and the systems around it. The lead does not build roles or configure GRC; specialists do. The lead decides what good looks like, sets the order of work, approves designs, chairs incidents, reports risk in numbers and answers the auditor. On a controls project the lead is also the bridge between the testers, who find access deficiencies, and the people who must fix them.

Role design standard and naming; which legacy roles go
A role's menu, authorisation values and organisational levels
Rule set changes and when a conflict is mitigated instead of removed
An ARA report and a mitigation record
How access reviews run and who reviews
Priority, communication and fix route in an access incident
Run SU53 or a trace personally
SU53, a trace summary and a transport log
A joiner-mover-leaver flow and an admin list

sections.title: 0.2 Your place in the Corvane project

blocks.text: 0.2 Your place in the Corvane project

You are Amara Osei. You join the Corvane controls project in week 9, on 9 March 2026, as the first access findings arrive. You report to Daniel Reyes, the Controls Lead. Your sponsor is Raymond Okafor, the CIO. You work every day with Neil Abernathy (IT Security Manager), Viktor Hale (Basis Lead), Lena Varga (GRC Administrator), Tom Brennan (Corporate IAM Manager) and Grace Mbeki (HR Systems Manager). Your team is six people: two security analysts, a shared GRC administrator, a role designer, an identity analyst and a shared Basis contact.

sections.title: Module 2 — SAP Authorisation Foundations and Troubleshooting

blocks.text: Module 2 — SAP Authorisation Foundations and Troubleshooting
Six sessions, about eight hours. By the end you can explain how SAP decides whether a user may do something, read the tools that show why it said no, and insist that the fix is controlled.

rows: The user master and user types

sections.title: Session 2.1 — How an Authorisation Check Works

blocks.text: Session 2.1 — How an Authorisation Check Works

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Describe the chain from user to role to authorisation object. Explain the two checks behind most transactions. Read an authorisation value: object, field and value.

blocks.text: 2.1.1 The chain

A user holds roles. Each role generates a profile, and the profile contains authorisations. An authorisation is a set of permitted values for one authorisation object. An authorisation object groups up to ten fields that SAP checks together, for example the company code and the activity. The program asks the question in code (the ABAP statement AUTHORITY-CHECK) and the system answers yes or no from the user's buffer of authorisations.
User → Role (PFCG) → Profile → Authorisation → Object, fields and values
2.1.2 Two checks behind most transactions

When a user starts a transaction, SAP first checks the start authorisation (object S_TCODE, field TCD). Inside the program, it then checks the business objects, such as F_BKPF_BUK for postings in a company code. A user can be allowed to start a transaction and still be refused at the first business check. In Fiori the start check is replaced by the launchpad and OData service checks (Module 4), but the back-end business checks are the same.

rows: May start the G/L journal entry transaction
Change tables in authorisation group SS (sensitive)

blocks.text: Activity codes are worth learning: 01 create, 02 change, 03 display, 06 delete. A value of * means every value. Most access findings come down to a * where a real value should be, or to a sensitive object in a role that does not need it.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane finance users post journals through the Fiori app Post General Journal Entries. Behind it they need the back-end object F_BKPF_BUK with activity 01 and their own company code. Derived role ZC_FI_GL_JE_D3000 (ROLE-035 in S01) carries company code 3000; on 8 April a change removed that value and 14 users were refused (INC-01).

PM LENS An authorisation check is like a gate review with a checklist: the gate does not care how senior you are, only whether every item on the list is present. A missing value fails the gate exactly as a missing sign-off would.
TRY IT 2.1 In S01 Role_Catalogue, find the master role for journal entry and its four derived roles. What differs between them, and what is the same?

sections.title: Session 2.2 — The User Master and User Types

blocks.text: Session 2.2 — The User Master and User Types

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the five SAP user types and which can log on in dialog. Explain why default users matter to auditors. Read the default and job user findings in S01.

blocks.text: 2.2.1 User types

rows: Named, one person each; no sharing
Extra authorisations added to other users

blocks.text: Only system, communication and reference users cannot log on in dialog. A service user can, which is why service users with broad access are a finding.
2.2.2 Default and standard users

Every SAP system ships with powerful default users. SAP* exists in the kernel; if its master record is deleted and the profile parameter login/no_automatic_user_sapstar is not 1, anyone can log on as SAP* with the well-known password. DDIC owns the data dictionary and holds SAP_ALL. Both must be locked, with changed passwords, in every client, and used only through the emergency access process. TMSADM is the transport communication user. Auditors test these every year.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE S01 Default_and_Job_Users lists 25 users. SAP* and DDIC are locked in clients 100, 200, 300 and 400 but not in the training client 210 (two findings). Of fourteen background job users in CEP, three hold SAP_ALL: BATCH_BASIS, BATCH_ADMIN and BATCH_HR_PAY (three findings). No dialog user here: those are in DEF-001.
PM LENS Default users are like master keys handed over with a new building. Nobody owns them, everyone assumes someone else changed the locks.
TRY IT 2.2 Explain to Viktor Hale, in three sentences, why an unlocked SAP* in a training client matters when the client has only masked data.

blocks.text: Check yourself

3. Why is a job user with SAP_ALL a risk even though nobody logs on with it?

sections.title: Session 2.3 — Roles, Profiles and Powerful Profiles

blocks.text: Session 2.3 — Roles, Profiles and Powerful Profiles

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain the difference between a role and a profile. Name the profiles that bypass security. Say why profiles are never assigned directly.

blocks.text: 2.3.1 Roles and profiles

A role is built in transaction PFCG: a menu of transactions and apps, the authorisation values that go with them, and the users who hold it. When the role is saved, SAP generates a profile, which is what the system actually checks. Profiles can also be assigned directly to users in SU01. Direct profile assignment bypasses the role model, its owner and GRC, so it is allowed only for the emergency and technical exceptions your standard names.
2.3.2 Powerful profiles

rows: All checks added by new releases; grows at each upgrade
Change values while a program runs, bypassing any control

IN THE CORVANE CASE DEF-001 recorded nine dialog users with SAP_ALL in CEP and four generic IDs. ADR-03 (23 March 2026) removed SAP_ALL from dialog users and replaced generic IDs with named firefighter IDs. KPI-01 in S06 shows the count falling from 9 in March to 0 in July.
PM LENS SAP_ALL is a blank purchase order signed in advance. The question is never whether the holder is trustworthy but whether anyone could prove what they did.
TRY IT 2.3 Read KPI-01 and KPI-02 in S06. Write the two-line message you would give the CFO at the end of May about privileged access.

sections.title: Session 2.4 — Seeing Who Has What: SUIM

blocks.text: Session 2.4 — Seeing Who Has What: SUIM

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the SUIM reports a lead asks for. Explain why the population for a test or review starts from the system. Reconcile two counts of users.

blocks.text: 2.4.1 The reports

rows: Roles by complex criteria; table AGR_USERS
RSUSR002 (users by complex criteria, by transaction and authorisation values)
Privileged access lists; SoD checks without GRC
Where-used lists for objects and values

blocks.text: 2.4.2 Counts must agree

Two tools rarely give the same number. SUIM counts users in one client; GRC ARA counts users it has synchronised; HR counts people. Before any campaign or test, the lead asks for both counts and the reason for any gap. A gap is often the first sign of a broken connector or a population problem.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE CEP has 1,291 dialog users (S01 CF-06), and the Q2 access review covered 1,291 users (S04). From 6 April to 18 May the GRC sync to BW failed (CONN-02, INC-03) and ARA showed 41 BW users against 168 expected. A simple count reconciliation would have caught it weeks earlier.
PM LENS This is baseline control: you would never report progress against a plan you had not reconciled to the scope. Never report access against a population you have not reconciled to the system.
TRY IT 2.4 Write the request you would send to Lena Varga for the Q3 access review population, naming the reports and the reconciliation you expect.

Session 2.5 — Diagnosing a Missing Authorisation

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Classify an access failure before anyone touches a role. Know what SU53 and STAUTHTRACE show and miss. Spot a diagnosis that does not hold.

blocks.text: 2.5.1 Classify first

rows: "You are not authorised to use transaction"
Message inside the transaction; often an org value
Tile missing, app empty, works in GUI
Front-end and back-end trace; gateway error log
User in the wrong company code or screen
Ask the user to repeat it

blocks.text: 2.5.2 The tools

SU53 shows the last failed authorisation check for a user: object, fields and the values checked against what the user holds. It is fast and often enough. It misses a lot: only the last failure is kept, later checks can overwrite it, it can show a check that the program handled and did not matter, and in Fiori the failure may be on another server.

STAUTHTRACE (the system trace for authorisation checks) records every check for a user while the user repeats the task, on all application servers. It shows successful and failed checks in order, so the analyst can see the real failure and avoid adding values that were never needed.
SU53 (user 100458): Object F_BKPF_BUK  Field BUKRS  Checked: 3000  User has: 1000, 2000, 4000
2.5.3 Fixes that are not fixes
Adding * to a field to make the error go away.
Assigning SAP_ALL or a firefighter ID for daily work.
Copying a colleague's roles ("give her what he has").
Changing the role directly in production.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE INC-01 (8 April): SU53 showed F_BKPF_BUK failing for company code 3000; the role comparison showed RCH-004, imported the day before, had dropped the value. INC-02 (22 April) looked like a missing authorisation but was not: the user held a legacy role and a new composite with different company codes and ran the payment program from the wrong one. No role was changed. Read both in S05 Incidents and Diagnosis.
PM LENS This is defect triage. You would not let a developer patch production before the defect is reproduced and classified. Access is the same.

TRY IT 2.5 A buyer says: "I can create purchase orders but cannot release them since yesterday." List your first three questions and the tool for each. Then read DEF-030 in W13: why might "fixing" this be the wrong answer?

sections.title: Session 2.6 — Controlled Fixes and Incident Records

blocks.text: Session 2.6 — Controlled Fixes and Incident Records

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES State the route of a controlled access fix. Know when emergency access is right. Write an incident record an auditor can follow.

blocks.text: 2.6.1 The route
Diagnose → change role in DEV → test in QAS → ARA simulation → owner approval → transport → confirm with the user

Every step leaves evidence: the request, the test, the simulation result, the approval and the transport. When the business cannot wait, emergency access through a firefighter ID with a reason code and a controller review is the right route, not a direct change. The role fix still follows the route afterwards.
2.6.2 The incident record

rows: Shows the cause was proven, not guessed
Fix and linked keys (role, change, connector)

IN THE CORVANE CASE S05 holds nine incidents with 24 diagnosis steps. Each links to a role, a role change or a connector. INC-09, the quarter-end outage, followed this route under pressure: previous role versions were rebuilt in DEV, checked by a second person, simulated in ARA, approved by the CIO and imported (Module 10 covers it fully).
PM LENS An incident record is a mini lessons-learned log. If it cannot be read by someone who was not there, it has not been written.
TRY IT 2.6 Using S05 for INC-06, write the five-line summary you would put in the monthly metrics pack.

sections.title: Module 3 — Role Design, Lifecycle and Least Privilege

blocks.text: Module 3 — Role Design, Lifecycle and Least Privilege
Seven sessions, about ten hours. By the end you can judge a role model, run a role change through a governed lifecycle, and lead a least-privilege programme without breaking the business.

rows: Master roles, derived roles and organisational levels

sections.title: Session 3.1 — Role Design as Business Design

blocks.text: Session 3.1 — Role Design as Business Design

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain why roles start from tasks, not transactions. Name the principles of a sound role model. Describe the Corvane catalogue in numbers.

blocks.text: A role model is a business design. Each role should answer the question "which task does this let someone do, in which part of the company?" A model built that way can be reviewed by the business, analysed for conflicts and kept small. A model built by copying users' access ("make her like him") grows without end and nobody can review it.

rows: Roles grant tasks (post an invoice), not job titles
Only what the task needs, with real organisational values
No single role grants both sides of a conflict
A business owner approves content and assignments
Company code, plant, purchasing organisation set per derived role
Description, owner, risks and test cases on record

IN THE CORVANE CASE The CEP catalogue holds 418 single roles (96 master, 248 derived, 74 standalone) and 41 composites for 1,291 users (S01 Catalogue_Facts). S01 Role_Catalogue is a 100-role sample: 24 masters, 48 derived for company codes 1000 to 4000, 16 standalone (10 legacy) and 12 composites.
PM LENS A role model is a work breakdown structure for access. If the tasks are wrong, every estimate, review and control built on it is wrong too.
TRY IT 3.1 From S01, pick one composite role and describe in plain words the job it serves and any conflict it carries.

sections.title: Session 3.2 — Master Roles, Derived Roles and Organisational Levels

blocks.text: Session 3.2 — Master Roles, Derived Roles and Organisational Levels

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain how a derived role inherits from its master. Name common organisational levels. See how one master change reaches many users.

blocks.text: A master role holds the menu and authorisation values for a task, with the organisational levels left open. Each derived role copies everything from the master except the organisational levels, which are set per company code, plant or other unit. A change to the master is pushed to every derived role. That is the strength of the design (one change, consistent access) and its risk (one mistake, many users).

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Twelve masters in the S01 sample have four derived roles each (for example ZC_FI_GL_JE_M and ZC_FI_GL_JE_D1000 to D4000). On 30 September an emergency transport (RCH-040) overwrote company-code values in 18 derived finance roles, and one master was changed as well, so company code 2000 still failed after the first fix (S05 War_Room_Timeline, 13:20).
PM LENS A master role is a template plan copied into each project. A template error repeats in every copy, so templates get the strictest change control.
TRY IT 3.2 Explain to Priya Raman why the second failure in company code 2000 happened and what check would have caught it before import.

sections.title: Session 3.3 — Composite Roles and Job Design

blocks.text: Session 3.3 — Composite Roles and Job Design

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain what a composite role is for. See how composites create conflicts. Decide when a composite needs a mitigation.

blocks.text: A composite role bundles single roles for a job, such as AP supervisor. It makes assignment simple: one approval, one role. It also hides risk: two harmless single roles can combine into a conflict, so every composite must be analysed as a whole, and any conflict either designed out or covered by a mitigating control in W06.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Five of the twelve composites in S01 carry a conflict by design: AP supervisor (SOD-005), financial controller (SOD-007), warehouse clerk (SOD-010), treasury analyst (SOD-012) and JV accountant (SOD-014). Each is covered in W06 Mitigations (MIT-03, MIT-04, MIT-07, MIT-08 and MIT-10). The other seven carry none.
PM LENS A composite is a package deal. Read every line of the contract, not just the cover page.
TRY IT 3.3 For the treasury analyst composite, state the conflict, why the business may accept it, and what the mitigating control must prove.

Session 3.4 — Naming, Ownership and Documentation

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Read the Corvane naming standard. Explain what a role owner does. Spot an unowned role and act on it.

blocks.text: A naming standard lets anyone read a role's purpose and type from its name. Corvane's standard is ZC_<area>_<function>_<type>, where the type is M (master), D plus company code (derived), S (standalone single) or C (composite, written ZC_C_<job>). Legacy roles from ECC start with Z_ and are being retired.
ZC_FI_AP_INV_D2000   = finance, AP invoice entry, derived for company code 2000

A role owner is a business manager who approves what the role contains, approves who gets it, and reviews it each year. Without an owner nobody can approve a change or a review, so an unowned role is either given an owner or frozen.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Two legacy roles have no owner (TBC): Z_FI_UPLOAD (linked to DEF-017, the journal upload program) and Z_PS_SETTLE. Both are flagged in S01 with notes. DEF-026 shows the cost of weak ownership: two of 25 sampled assignments were approved by the line manager only.
PM LENS An unowned role is an unowned deliverable. You would not sign off a deliverable that has no accountable owner.
TRY IT 3.4 Draft the email asking the Group Financial Controller to name an owner for Z_FI_UPLOAD by a date, stating what happens if no owner is named.

sections.title: Session 3.5 — The Role Lifecycle and BRM

blocks.text: Session 3.5 — The Role Lifecycle and BRM

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES State the stages of the role lifecycle. Explain what GRC Business Role Management adds. Read the role change register.
Does a role already do this?
What task, which values, which owner?
Does it create a conflict or critical access?
Does it work and does it refuse what it should?
Positive and negative test in QAS
Did it reach PRD as tested?

blocks.text: Business Role Management (BRM) in GRC Access Control runs these stages as a workflow with the risk analysis and approvals built in, so the evidence is produced as the work is done. Without BRM, the same steps rely on discipline and checklists.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane adopted BRM for role changes from 1 June 2026 (ADR-02). S01 Role_Changes holds 40 changes. Before June, changes went through ChaRM only and several had no ARA simulation; each carries a transition note. After June every change has owner approval and a simulation. RCH-040 shows what the lifecycle prevents when it is skipped: an emergency import without a QAS test.
PM LENS The role lifecycle is a stage-gate process for a very small product. The gates are cheap; skipping them is not.
TRY IT 3.5 Count the changes in S01 imported without an ARA simulation, and write one sentence for the auditor explaining how the transition was handled.

sections.title: Session 3.6 — Least Privilege and Usage Analysis

blocks.text: Session 3.6 — Least Privilege and Usage Analysis

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the main sources of excess access. Use usage data safely. Set and report a least-privilege target.

blocks.text: Access grows: roles are copied, values set to * to make a problem go away, legacy roles kept "just in case", and movers keep old roles. Usage data (transaction statistics, ST03N) shows which transactions in a role were actually used. It is strong evidence for removal, with care: some tasks run once a year (year-end close, annual depreciation), so use at least twelve months, and agree removals with the owner.

rows: Z_ roles still assigned after conversion
Old roles kept after a job change

IN THE CORVANE CASE 37 percent of the transactions in assigned roles were never used in 12 months (CF-09); the target is about half of that, 19 percent in S06, by 31 December 2026. KPI-09 in S06 shows 37 in March falling to 33 in September. The S01 sample shows 43 percent because it contains every legacy role; always quote the catalogue figure.
PM LENS This is scope reduction with a cost-benefit test: every removal must save more risk than the disruption it causes.
TRY IT 3.6 Why is 33 percent in September still "Not met" in S06, and what pace is needed to reach the target by year end?

sections.title: Session 3.7 — Authorisation Defaults and Migration Residue

blocks.text: Session 3.7 — Authorisation Defaults and Migration Residue

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain SU24 authorisation defaults. Describe what SU25 does after an upgrade or conversion. Plan the clean-up of migration residue.

blocks.text: SU24 holds the authorisation defaults for each transaction or app: which objects it checks and with which proposed values. When a role designer adds a transaction in PFCG, these defaults bring the right objects into the role. After an upgrade or conversion, SU25 compares SAP's new defaults with the customer's and identifies roles whose authorisations need checking (steps 2a to 2c), then transports the adjusted defaults (step 2d). If this is skipped, roles carry old values: they fail where new checks exist, or someone fills the gap with broad manual values.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane converted from ECC 6.0 to S/4HANA 2023 on 10 March 2025 (FX-01), the "2025 upgrade" in the case file. SU25 steps 2c and 2d were not completed, and 112 roles still hold outdated defaults (CF-10). In S01, roles with "SU24 defaults current" set to N are the candidates. Combined with the 63 legacy roles held by 214 users, this residue is why ADR-04 redesigns rather than patches.
PM LENS Migration residue is technical debt. Like any debt, it is paid back on a plan, with the most expensive items first.
TRY IT 3.7 Draft a three-line plan to Viktor Hale and Neil Abernathy for finishing SU25 and refreshing the 112 roles, with the order you would do it in and why.

rows: ZC_FI_GL_JE_M (master) and D1000, D2000, D3000, D4000 share the same menu and authorisation values; only the company-code value differs. Each derived role is assigned to that company code's users.

Module 4 — Fiori and S/4HANA Security

Six sessions, about eight hours. By the end you can explain what an S/4HANA conversion does to access, read the Fiori access chain from tile to table, and keep Fiori and migration changes under the same control as any role change.

sections.title: Session 4.1 — Why Migration Security Is More Than Role Conversion

blocks.text: Session 4.1 — Why Migration Security Is More Than Role Conversion

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the three migration approaches and what each means for roles. Explain why a technically working conversion can leave access unsafe. Place Corvane's conversion in context.
New role model designed from scratch
Existing ECC system converted in place
Existing roles carried over; adjusted, not redesigned
New system shell; chosen data and configuration moved
Mixed: some roles reused, some redesigned

blocks.text: A conversion is judged a success when the business can post on day one. That test says nothing about whether users can do too much. Roles carried over from ECC keep transactions that no longer exist, values that were broad to begin with, and conflicts nobody analysed for the new apps. The access risk of a conversion shows up months later, in audit findings and in users who still hold the old way of working alongside the new.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane converted from ECC 6.0 EhP8 to S/4HANA 2023 by brownfield conversion, live on 10 March 2025 (FX-01): the "2025 upgrade" that W13 and the Corvane Story refer to. Roles were carried over and adjusted. A year later the residue is still there: 63 legacy Z_ roles held by 214 users, 112 roles with outdated authorisation defaults, and 37 percent of role content unused (S01 Catalogue_Facts).
PM LENS A conversion that goes live on time but leaves access unreviewed is a project that moved its risk into operations. The lead's job is to show where it went.
TRY IT 4.1 In three sentences for the CIO, explain why the 2025 conversion still drives access findings in 2026.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What happens to roles in a brownfield conversion?
2. Why is "users can post on day one" not a security test?

sections.title: Session 4.2 — What S/4HANA Changes for Access

blocks.text: Session 4.2 — What S/4HANA Changes for Access

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain the business partner change and why it matters for SoD. Recognise obsolete and replaced transactions in old roles. Say why the rule set must follow the new design.

blocks.text: 4.2.1 The business partner

In S/4HANA the business partner (transaction BP) replaces separate vendor and customer master maintenance. The old transactions largely redirect to BP. Business partner authorisations use their own objects (for example B_BUPA_GRP for authorisation groups and B_BUPA_RLT for roles such as supplier or customer). A rule set that still looks only for the old vendor master transactions will miss a user who changes supplier bank details through BP.
4.2.2 Simplification and changed functions

SAP publishes a simplification list for each release. Some transactions are removed, some replaced by new ones or by Fiori apps, and some functions move to new objects. For access this means: old roles hold transactions that do nothing, new functions may be missing from roles and from the rule set, and the conflict analysis must be redone for the new paths.

rows: Vendor and customer master into BP
New objects; old checks miss the risk
Does the rule set check BP for bank detail changes?
Do SoD rules cover both paths?
Clutter in roles; false comfort in reviews
Have they been removed from roles?

IN THE CORVANE CASE The S02 rule set includes the critical action "Change vendor bank details (FK02, BP)", added after the conversion so that bank detail changes are caught on both paths. SOD-001 (create or change a vendor and run the payment) has the most conflicts in the Q2 run, 88, of which 19 were false positives.
PM LENS This is like a re-baselined plan: the old tasks are renamed and merged, so every report built on the old task list has to be checked before anyone trusts it.

Session 4.3 — Fiori in Layers

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the layers between a tile and a posting. Explain catalogues, spaces and pages, and business roles. Describe the Corvane hub deployment.

blocks.text: Fiori access is layered. The launchpad shows what a user may see; the app needs a service the user may call; the back end decides what the user may do. A user can fail at any layer, and a role that fixes one layer does not fix the others.

rows: Business catalogues (sets of apps: tile plus target mapping); spaces and pages (the layout the user sees, replacing the older groups)
A PFCG role on the front end that carries catalogues, spaces and pages
The OData service each app calls
The same objects as SAP GUI, such as F_BKPF_BUK

blocks.text: Corvane runs a hub deployment: a separate Fiori front-end server (FEP, SYS-05) in front of the S/4HANA back end (CEP, SYS-03). Each Fiori user therefore needs a front-end role and a back-end role that match.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane uses 46 business catalogues and 9 spaces (S01 CF-11 and CF-12). The base front-end role ZC_FIORI_BASE_S (S01) is held by all 1,291 users; task access comes from roles paired with back-end roles such as ZC_FI_AP_INV_D1000.

PM LENS Think of a delivery: the shop window (launchpad), the order desk (service) and the warehouse (back end). An order can fail at any of the three, and fixing the window does not fill the warehouse.
TRY IT 4.3 A user says "the tile is there but the app is empty". Which layer do you suspect first, and why?

3. Why does a hub deployment need paired roles?

sections.title: Session 4.4 — OData Services and the Two-Server Check

blocks.text: Session 4.4 — OData Services and the Two-Server Check

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain why access can work in SAP GUI and fail in Fiori. Name the tools that show a Fiori failure. Read INC-06 as a worked case.

blocks.text: Each Fiori app calls one or more OData services. The service must be activated on the front-end server, and the user must be authorised to call it (object S_SERVICE). The back end then runs the same business checks as SAP GUI. So a user with perfect back-end access can still see an empty app if the service is not active or not in the front-end role, and SU53 on the back end will show nothing wrong.

rows: Catalogue or space not in the front-end role
Tile opens, no data or error
Service not active or not authorised

IN THE CORVANE CASE INC-06 (9 July): an AP supervisor could approve journals in SAP GUI but the Fiori app showed no data. The front-end trace showed no failed check; the gateway error log showed three OData services for the journal apps not activated in production (FX-06). They were activated through a transported change and S_SERVICE values were added to the role ZC_FI_GL_REL_M. Nine users were affected; service was restored the next day (S05).
PM LENS When a test passes in one environment and fails in another, you compare environments, not people. GUI against Fiori is the same comparison.
TRY IT 4.4 Write the three-step diagnosis you would expect an analyst to follow for INC-06, naming the tool at each step.

sections.title: Session 4.5 — Designing Fiori Access from a Persona

blocks.text: Session 4.5 — Designing Fiori Access from a Persona

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Design access from a persona's tasks. Keep front-end and back-end roles aligned. Avoid the most common Fiori design mistakes.

blocks.text: Persona → tasks → apps → catalogues → spaces and pages → front-end role → back-end role with organisational values

Start from the persona: what the person does each day, week and month. Map tasks to apps, apps to catalogues, and build the space the user sees. Then build or reuse the back-end role that grants the same tasks with the right organisational values. Name the pair so anyone can see they belong together, and analyse them together for conflicts.

rows: Users see and can call far more apps than they need
Build task catalogues from the apps the persona needs
Front-end role without a matching back-end role
Tiles that fail; pressure to add broad back-end access
Design and test the pair together
Risk analysis on back-end roles only

IN THE CORVANE CASE The Corvane AP clerk persona (composite ZC_C_AP_CLERK) needs supplier invoice entry and display apps in company codes 1000 to 4000. The front-end content sits in a task catalogue for invoice entry; the back-end access comes from the derived roles ZC_FI_AP_INV_D1000 to D4000. The AP supervisor persona adds approval and carries SOD-005, covered by mitigation MIT-03 in W06.
PM LENS A persona is a requirements document for access. Without one, the design is a guess and every test is an argument.

blocks.text: A change to a catalogue or a space changes what users can reach, so it follows the same lifecycle as a role change (Module 3). Activating an OData service in production is a change too. Both are sensitive and belong in the rule set as critical actions, so that anyone who can do them is visible.

Seven sessions, about ten hours. By the end you can direct the GRC administrator: judge rule set quality, read an ARA result, design workflow that does not stall, govern emergency access, and notice when GRC is working on stale data.

sections.title: Session 5.1 — GRC Access Control at Corvane

blocks.text: Session 5.1 — GRC Access Control at Corvane

blocks.text: Corvane runs GRC Access Control 12.0 SP22 on premise (GRP, SYS-04), connected to CEP, BWP, FEP and CEQ. The lead owns the decisions: what the rule set must detect, when a conflict is mitigated, how requests route, who may hold emergency access and how often each is reviewed. The GRC administrator configures them.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE ADR-01 (14 April 2026) kept GRC 12.0 on premise for the SAP systems and set an assessment of SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance (IAG) for the cloud applications in FY2027 (S06).
PM LENS GRC is a programme management office for access: it holds the rules, the requests, the exceptions and the reviews. Its outputs are only as good as the data and the rules it is given.

sections.title: Session 5.2 — The Rule Set: Risks, Functions, Actions and Permissions

blocks.text: Session 5.2 — The Rule Set: Risks, Functions, Actions and Permissions

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain how a rule set is built. Distinguish SoD risks from critical actions and permissions. Judge a rule set's quality.

blocks.text: Risk → functions → actions (transactions, apps) → permissions (objects and values) → generated rules

A risk describes a business danger, such as "create a vendor and pay it". It is made of functions (vendor maintenance; payment run). Each function lists actions (the transactions and apps that perform it) and permissions (the authorisation objects and values that really allow it). GRC generates rules from every combination. An SoD risk needs two or more functions; a critical action or permission risk needs only one, because holding it alone is dangerous.

rows: Every risk maps to a business risk in the risk register
Conflicts can be explained to an owner
Permissions, not just actions, are defined
New paths (BP, Fiori apps) are included
Organisational rules where functions differ by company code
Changes go through BRM with audit informed

IN THE CORVANE CASE CORVANE_RS was copied from the SAP standard rule set in 2019. It holds 54 risks: 16 SoD risks that map one for one to SOD-001 to SOD-016 in W06, and 38 critical action and permission risks, ten of them linked to SENS-001 to SENS-010 (S02 Rule_Set).
PM LENS The rule set is the acceptance criteria for access. Weak criteria pass bad work and fail good work; both waste the team's time.
TRY IT 5.2 Take SOD-011 (change bank accounts and run payments). List the two functions and one action and one permission you would expect in each.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is a function in a rule set?

sections.title: Session 5.3 — Reading ARA: Levels, False Positives and Organisational Rules

blocks.text: Session 5.3 — Reading ARA: Levels, False Positives and Organisational Rules

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Read a user-level and a role-level ARA result. Explain false positives and their cost. Know when organisational rules help.

blocks.text: ARA can analyse at action level (does the user hold the transactions?) or permission level (does the user hold the objects and values that really allow it?). Permission level is slower and more accurate. Role-level analysis shows conflicts built into roles; user-level shows what each person really holds across all roles. Simulation runs the analysis before a change, which is how BRM and ARM prevent new conflicts.

A false positive is a reported conflict that is not real, for example because the user can post in company code 1000 and pay only in company code 3000. False positives cost reviewer time and, worse, train owners to ignore the report. Organisational rules let ARA compare the organisational values of the conflicting functions, so that conflicts across different company codes drop out where the business accepts that.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE In the Q2 2026 run CORVANE_RS reported 889 conflicts, 196 of them false: 22 percent (S02). The worst rule by share is SOD-014 (equity shares and JV billing): 15 of 26 conflicts false, because no organisational rule exists for company code 2000, the joint venture operations code (RULE-014 note). ADR-05 (23 June) set organisational rules for 2000 and a review of the ten noisiest rules; KPI-07 falls from 26 percent in March to 16 in September against a target of 10.
PM LENS False positives are noise in a status report. When half the red items are not really red, nobody reads the red items.
TRY IT 5.3 From S02 Rule_Set, list the three SoD rules with the most false positives by count and the three with the highest share. Which list should drive the clean-up, and why?

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is the difference between action and permission level?
2. Why are false positives harmful beyond wasted time?
3. What do organisational rules compare?

sections.title: Session 5.4 — Access Requests: ARM, MSMP and BRF+

blocks.text: Session 5.4 — Access Requests: ARM, MSMP and BRF+

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Describe how a request moves through GRC. Explain MSMP paths, stages and BRF+ agent rules. Design workflow that cannot stall.

blocks.text: A request in ARM (new user, add or remove roles, lock, unlock) is routed by the multi-stage, multi-path workflow (MSMP). A BRF+ rule decides the path, and at each stage an agent rule finds the approver: the line manager, the role owner, the process owner. Risk analysis runs inside the request, so an approver sees any conflict before approving. After the last approval GRC provisions the access to the target system.

rows: Every agent rule has a fallback agent
A request never waits for someone who left
A risk path for unmitigated conflicts
Senior approval for real risk, not for every request

IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane has four paths (S02 Workflow_Paths): new user, change access, a risk path, and lock or remove for leavers and movers from SailPoint (automatic). In May a role owner left; the agent rule on WF-02 returned no approver and had no fallback, so 23 requests waited 11 days (INC-04). A fallback agent was added on 2 June. Average provisioning time (KPI-10) went from 4.6 days in May to 2.6 in September.
PM LENS Workflow is a RACI made executable. A RACI with a vacancy in the A column stops the work; so does an agent rule with no fallback.
TRY IT 5.4 Write two monitoring checks the GRC administrator should run weekly so that INC-04 cannot happen unnoticed again.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What does a BRF+ agent rule decide?
2. Why must every agent rule have a fallback?
3. Why can removal requests skip approval?
Session 5.5 — Emergency Access: EAM

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain how firefighter access works. Name the roles of owner, controller and firefighter. Judge an emergency access review.

blocks.text: Emergency access lets a named person take on a powerful firefighter ID for a short time, with a reason code. Every session is logged (transactions used, changes made, the security audit log), and a controller reviews the log afterwards. The firefighter ID has an owner who decides who may use it; the controller must be someone else. The review is the control: an unreviewed session is privileged access with a paper trail nobody read.

rows: Decides who may use the firefighter ID; reviews the assignment
Uses the ID only for the stated reason; records what was done
Reviews every session log promptly and questions anything unusual

IN THE CORVANE CASE Corvane has six firefighter IDs and seven reason codes (S02). Two IDs, FF-05 and FF-06, are used by support partners. DEF-005 recorded four of 25 sessions reviewed after more than five business days, and two reviews that did not question unusual activity, including a vendor bank change. KPI-04 shows on-time reviews rising from 84 percent in March to 100 percent from July. INC-07 (28 July) shows why log collection is monitored: one session log did not arrive and was rebuilt from SM20.
PM LENS Emergency access is a change freeze exception. Exceptions are fine; unreviewed exceptions are how freezes fail.
TRY IT 5.5 Write the three questions a controller should ask about a firefighter session in which a vendor's bank details were changed.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. Why must owner and controller differ?
2. What does the controller review?
3. Why is log collection monitored?
Session 5.6 — Connectors and Synchronisation

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain what a GRC connector is and what synchronisation does. Name the main sync jobs. Notice when GRC is working on stale data.

blocks.text: GRC reaches each system through a connector built on an RFC destination and a technical user. Synchronisation jobs copy into GRC what it needs to analyse: users, roles and profiles (repository object sync), authorisations (authorisation sync), usage (action and role usage sync), and firefighter logs. If a sync fails, GRC keeps working on old data and its reports look normal. That is the danger.

rows: The objects and values in roles
Which transactions and roles were used

IN THE CORVANE CASE On 6 April the RFC password for the BW connector changed and the repository sync to BWP failed silently until 18 May (CONN-02, INC-03, FX-09). For six weeks ARA under-reported BW users: 41 against 168 expected. A weekly check of the last successful sync date per connector, now in S02 Connectors, would have caught it in days.
PM LENS Stale data is the most dangerous status report: green, confident and wrong.
TRY IT 5.6 Draft a one-line weekly control for connector health and say who performs it and who reviews it.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What does a connector consist of?
2. What does repository object sync bring into GRC?
3. Why is a failed sync dangerous?
Session 5.7 — Security Logging

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain the security audit log and table logging. Read a logging settings register. Know why logging is the base of every review.

blocks.text: The security audit log (SM20 to read; SM19 or RSAU_CONFIG to configure; switched on with the parameter rsau/enable) records logons, failed logons, transaction starts and other security events by filter. Table logging (parameter rec/client, with tables flagged for logging) records changes to configuration and control tables, read with SCU3. Firefighter reviews, investigations and many ITGC tests depend on both. If they are off, there is nothing to review.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE S02 Logging lists six settings. The security audit log is active in CEP and GRC, with a filter for all users and critical events. Table logging is on in CEP 300 but off in CEQ 200 (LG-04): changes to test configuration are not logged. Because transports move configuration from QAS onwards, the lead asks for it to be switched on.
PM LENS Logging is the project's audit trail. You cannot reconstruct a decision that was never minuted.
TRY IT 5.7 Explain to Viktor Hale in two sentences why table logging in CEQ 200 matters even though it is not production.

sections.title: Module 6 — SoD, Critical Access, Mitigations and Access Reviews

blocks.text: Module 6 — SoD, Critical Access, Mitigations and Access Reviews

Seven sessions, about nine hours. By the end you can decide between removing and mitigating a conflict, judge a mitigating control, govern critical access, and run an access review that both the auditor and the business can trust.

rows: Segregation of duties: risk, conflict and technical path
Access reviews: population, reviewers and context
Running a campaign: decisions, rubber-stamping and removal

sections.title: Session 6.1 — Segregation of Duties: Risk, Conflict and Technical Path

blocks.text: Session 6.1 — Segregation of Duties: Risk, Conflict and Technical Path

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain SoD as a business risk, not a technical rule. Trace a conflict from risk to functions to access. Read the W06 SoD matrix.

blocks.text: Segregation of duties stops one person from completing a sensitive process alone, such as creating a vendor and paying it. Each SoD rule names two functions, the business risk they create together and the process it sits in. The technical path is how the user gets each function: a transaction or app, the objects and the values. A conflict is real only when one user holds both paths in the same organisational scope.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE W06 holds 20 functions (FN-01 to FN-20) and 16 SoD rules. SOD-001 pairs vendor master maintenance (FN-01) with the payment run (FN-02): "a user can create or change a vendor and run the payment, enabling fictitious vendor payments", rated Critical. The production rule set CORVANE_RS dates from 2019, but its 16 SoD risks were aligned in March 2026 to the project's matrix (W06 Ruleset_Version 0.9, approved by the Group Financial Controller on 13 March). That version excludes custom Z transactions, a gap the lead should close.
PM LENS SoD is the four-eyes principle you already use for budget approval: the person who raises the spend does not approve it.
TRY IT 6.1 Name one custom transaction in the Corvane case that a matrix without Z transactions would miss, and the risk it carries (hint: DEF-017).

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What does an SoD rule name?
2. When is a reported conflict real?
3. Why does excluding Z transactions matter?
Session 6.2 — Remediate First, Mitigate Second

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES List the ways to remove a conflict. Know when mitigation is the right answer. Track conflicts to a target.
Remove a role from the user
The user does not need one side
Business need is real and removal would stop the work

blocks.text: Mitigation accepts the risk and adds a control to catch misuse. It is the last option, not the first, because the risk stays and the control must work every period. Every mitigation needs an owner, an end date and a business reason.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE KPI-06 in S06 tracks users with an unmitigated SoD conflict: 61 in March, 16 in September, against a target of 10. Most of the fall came from retiring legacy all-in-one roles such as Z_FI_ALL (SOD-001 and SOD-006) and Z_MM_SUPER (SOD-003 and SOD-016) in S01, not from new mitigations.
PM LENS Mitigation is a risk accepted with a contingency plan. A risk log full of accepted risks is a plan that gave up on reducing them.
TRY IT 6.2 For a buyer who also creates vendors (SOD-016), list two removal options before mitigation, and the question you would ask the procurement manager.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. Name four ways to remove a conflict.
2. Why is mitigation the last option?
3. What must every mitigation have?

sections.title: Session 6.3 — Designing a Strong Mitigating Control

blocks.text: Session 6.3 — Designing a Strong Mitigating Control

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES State what makes a mitigating control strong. Read the W06 mitigation register. Challenge a weak mitigation.
Someone independent of the conflicted users
Every transaction where both sides were used, from a system report
A complete report with its own completeness check
Matches the risk (monthly or more for payments)
Signed, dated review with follow-up of each exception
Tested effective by the controls team

IN THE CORVANE CASE W06 Mitigations holds twelve mitigations (MIT-01 to MIT-12), all valid from 1 April to 31 December 2026, each approved by a business owner and each linked to a control tested effective. For example MIT-08 covers SOD-012 (bank master and bank reconciliation) for two treasury users with control C-BPC-TRE-002, approved by the Treasury Manager. Together the mitigations cover 73 users.
PM LENS A mitigating control is a quality gate placed after the work instead of before it. It is only as good as the inspector's independence and the completeness of what is inspected.
TRY IT 6.3 A manager proposes "I will review the payment run each month" as the mitigation for SOD-001. Rewrite it as a strong mitigating control.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. Why must the performer be independent?
2. Why does the population need its own completeness check?
3. What makes evidence acceptable?

sections.title: Session 6.4 — Critical Access and Privileged Users

blocks.text: Session 6.4 — Critical Access and Privileged Users

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain critical access and why it is listed separately from SoD. Read the W06 sensitive access list. Connect critical access to deficiencies and decisions.

blocks.text: Some access is dangerous on its own: SAP_ALL, debugging with replace, direct table change, user administration in production, transport import, running jobs as another user. These are critical actions and permissions. They are allowed only to named holders, usually through emergency access, and every holder must be on an approved list reviewed regularly.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE W06 Sensitive_Access lists ten items (SENS-001 to SENS-010) with their allowed holders; SAP_ALL, for example, is for firefighter IDs only, never dialog users. DEF-001 found nine dialog users with SAP_ALL and four generic IDs, rated a significant deficiency in group GR-A (privileged access governance). ADR-03 removed SAP_ALL from dialog users and moved emergency work to named firefighter IDs; KPI-01 reached zero in July.
PM LENS Critical access is the project's production change authority. You would not give it to everyone who might one day need it; you grant it per change, with a record.
TRY IT 6.4 From S01 Default_and_Job_Users, list the critical access that W06 does not yet cover because the holders are job users, and say how you would add it to the approved list.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is critical access?
2. Who may hold SAP_ALL at Corvane?
3. What did ADR-03 change?

sections.title: Session 6.5 — Access Reviews: Population, Reviewers and Context

blocks.text: Session 6.5 — Access Reviews: Population, Reviewers and Context

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES State the attributes of a sound access review. Choose reviewers and give them context. Reconcile the review population.

blocks.text: An access review (user access certification) asks the people who know the business to confirm that each user still needs each access. Its value depends on three things: a complete population, the right reviewer, and enough context for a real decision. A reviewer shown only role names will approve everything.

rows: A. Campaign listing complete (agrees to AGR_USERS)
Population reconciled to SUIM before launch
B. Every package reviewed by an authorised reviewer
Reviewer is the line manager or role owner, not a delegate of convenience
C. Review completed within the window
D. Rejected access removed within 10 business days
Removal dates against the due date

IN THE CORVANE CASE The Q1 2026 campaign showed reviewers role names only, and 81 percent finished on time. For Q2 the lead added role descriptions, 12-month usage and SoD flags. Q2 covered 1,291 users and 6,455 lines with 47 reviewers; 94 percent finished on time (S04 Campaigns). The control C-ITGC-AC-003 was tested and passed, and W13 treats it as the compensating control for the late leaver locks in DEF-010 (group GR-C).
PM LENS An access review is a stakeholder sign-off. Sign-offs on documents nobody can understand are worthless, however many signatures they carry.
TRY IT 6.5 List the four pieces of context you would show a line manager for each user-role line, and why each helps.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What three things decide an access review's value?
2. What does attribute A require?
3. Why did the Q2 design add usage data?

sections.title: Session 6.6 — Running a Campaign: Decisions, Rubber-Stamping and Removal

blocks.text: Session 6.6 — Running a Campaign: Decisions, Rubber-Stamping and Removal

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Read campaign statistics critically. Detect rubber-stamping. Prove that rejected access was removed.

blocks.text: A campaign can meet every test attribute and still be weak. The lead looks beyond completion: how long reviewers spent, how many lines each approved without question, and whether removals reached production in time. A reviewer who approves hundreds of lines in a few minutes has not reviewed them.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE In Q2, 39 lines were removed (0.6 percent), all through GRC requests and all within six business days of the due date, well inside attribute D's ten (S04 Decisions). Three line managers approved every line in under ten minutes: URV-07 (412 lines in 6 minutes), URV-19 (388 in 8) and URV-33 (301 in 9). The control test passed, so this is not a deficiency; it is a quality problem the lead acts on before an auditor finds it.
PM LENS Completion is not quality. A team that closes every task on time but never finds a defect is either perfect or not looking.
TRY IT 6.6 Draft the note to the three line managers and their directors, and the change you would make to the Q3 campaign so the pattern cannot repeat unnoticed.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. Why is on-time completion not enough?
2. What signals rubber-stamping?
3. How do you prove a removal happened?
Session 6.7 — Special Accounts in Reviews

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the accounts that ordinary reviews miss. Assign the right reviewer to each. Close the gaps at Corvane.
Not a person; no line manager
Basis Lead with the IT Security Manager
Owned by a project that ended
Sponsoring manager, with an end date

Outside it: six firefighter IDs (two used by support partners), fourteen job users (three with SAP_ALL), nine interface users in W02 (one of type Service: SFTP_PROD_SVC for production volumes), and nine contractors with no end date in SailPoint (JML-12, which led to INC-08).
PM LENS Every project has resources not on the org chart: contractors, vendors, shared services. They still need managing.

blocks.text: Module 7 — Identity and Cloud

Seven sessions, about nine hours. By the end you can map who a user is from the HR system to every SAP and cloud account, find where joiners, movers and leavers fall through, and govern single sign-on and cloud administrators.

rows: Attributes and access models: RBAC, ABAC, PBAC
Provisioning to the cloud: IPS and BTP
Cloud applications and their security models
Governance across SAP and cloud: the IAG decision

blocks.text: Session 7.1 — Identity, Account and Entitlement

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Distinguish identity, account and entitlement. Explain IAM and IGA. Read the Corvane identity landscape.
The person, once, with attributes from the HR system
The person's user in one system
User 100458 in CEP, the Entra ID account, the Ariba user
Roles in CEP; role collections in BTP
Identity and access management: authentication, accounts
Identity governance and administration: lifecycle, requests, certification

IN THE CORVANE CASE S03 Identity_Systems lists eight identity and cloud systems with IDS-IDs: SuccessFactors Employee Central (HR master since July 2025), SailPoint Identity Security Cloud, Microsoft Entra ID, SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS and IPS), Ariba Buying and Invoicing, the BTP subaccount and IAG (not deployed). None is in the FY2026 controls scope, which is why they take IDS-IDs and not SYS-IDs.
PM LENS Identity is the resource; accounts are the assignments; entitlements are the permissions on each assignment. One resource, many assignments, each to be closed when the resource leaves.
TRY IT 7.1 For one Corvane employee, list every account you would expect them to have from S03.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is the difference between an identity and an account?
2. What does IGA add to IAM?
3. Why do cloud systems take IDS-IDs?

sections.title: Session 7.2 — The Authoritative Source and Joiner-Mover-Leaver

blocks.text: Session 7.2 — The Authoritative Source and Joiner-Mover-Leaver

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Name the authoritative source and why it matters. Trace joiner, mover and leaver flows end to end. Find where each flow fails.

blocks.text: The authoritative source is the system whose word counts on whether a person works here, in which job and company. For employees it is the HR system. Every account should be created, changed and closed from events in that source. Where a flow is manual, slow or missing, accounts outlive their owners.

rows: EC → SailPoint (JML-02) → GRC ARM lock (JML-03) → CEP
Before 1 July 2026 a weekly HR report, the cause of DEF-010; late entry in EC still delays the lock
Old roles kept until the role owner acts
No end date for nine contractors; led to INC-08

IN THE CORVANE CASE DEF-010: six of 25 sampled leavers were locked after more than two business days, because the HR leavers report reached Security weekly. An interim daily report started on 4 May and the daily SailPoint feed through GRC went live on 1 July. KPI-03 (leavers locked on time) rose from 76 percent in March to 96 percent in August and September.
PM LENS A leaver is a project close-out: every access is a deliverable that must be handed back. A weekly batch means a week of open deliverables.
TRY IT 7.2 Write the mover rule you would propose for SailPoint, and the risk it removes.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is the authoritative source for employees?
2. What caused DEF-010?
3. Why do contractors need an end date?

sections.title: Session 7.3 — Attributes and Access Models: RBAC, ABAC, PBAC

blocks.text: Session 7.3 — Attributes and Access Models: RBAC, ABAC, PBAC

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain role-based, attribute-based and policy-based access. Read an attribute map. Say where each model fits at Corvane.
Rules on attributes (company code, job code)
Derived role chosen by company code; birthright access by job code
Central policies combine attributes and context
Entra group to BTP role collection mapping

blocks.text: Most enterprises run a hybrid: roles in SAP, with attributes choosing which role a person gets. Attributes only work if they are right in the source; a wrong job code in HR becomes wrong access everywhere.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE S03 Attribute_Map lists ten attributes, from employee ID (the correlation key) and employment status (the leaver trigger) to company code (selects the derived role) and worker type (sets the contractor end-date policy).
PM LENS Attributes are your resource data. Bad resource data gives a bad plan however good the scheduling engine is.
TRY IT 7.3 Pick two attributes from S03 and describe what goes wrong in SAP if each is wrong in SuccessFactors.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. How does ABAC decide access?
2. Why do most enterprises use a hybrid?
3. Which attribute triggers a leaver?
Session 7.4 — Federation and Single Sign-On

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain federation through an identity provider. Describe the Corvane IAS set-up. Know what SSO changes and what it does not.

blocks.text: With single sign-on the user signs in once at the corporate identity provider, which sends a signed statement (a SAML assertion) to each application. SAP Cloud Identity Services Identity Authentication (IAS) can act as a proxy: applications trust IAS, and IAS trusts the corporate identity provider. Password and multi-factor policy then live at the identity provider. SSO does not change what a user may do inside SAP; authorisations still come from roles.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE From 15 June 2026 Fiori logons go through IAS, which proxies Microsoft Entra ID (JML-07, JML-08; ADR-06). On day one, 86 users could not sign in: the name identifier was sent in mixed case and the Fiori user mapping is case sensitive (INC-05). SAP GUI password logon remains until Q1 2027, so the password parameters tested under C-ITGC-AC-006 still matter (DEF-011). KPI-12 shows SSO use rising from 58 percent in July to 93 percent in September.
PM LENS SSO is a single front door. It makes the house easier to enter and easier to lock, but it does not decide which rooms each person may go into.
TRY IT 7.4 Explain to the Group Financial Controller why SSO going live does not close DEF-011.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is a SAML assertion?
2. What does IAS do as a proxy?
3. What does SSO not change?

sections.title: Session 7.5 — Provisioning to the Cloud: IPS and BTP

blocks.text: Session 7.5 — Provisioning to the Cloud: IPS and BTP

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain what Identity Provisioning (IPS) does. Read the BTP administrator list. Spot access added outside the governed path.

blocks.text: SAP Cloud Identity Services Identity Provisioning (IPS) reads users and groups from a source, here Entra ID, and creates them in targets such as BTP, with group membership mapped to role collections. When provisioning is governed, an administrator added directly in the target is an exception to find and remove.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE IPS provisions users to the BTP subaccount CORVANE-PRD, which hosts Cloud Integration (SYS-08) and two extension apps (JML-09, JML-10). Two contractor platform administrators were added directly in the BTP cockpit, outside IPS; one has no MFA and neither has a review on record (S03 Cloud_Admins CA-03 and CA-04). ADR-07 (25 August) requires all cloud administrators to come through IPS and be certified in SailPoint, with direct admins removed by 30 November.
PM LENS Provisioning outside the governed path is like a contractor added to the project without a purchase order: it may be fine, but nobody can prove it.
TRY IT 7.5 Write the two checks you would run monthly on BTP until ADR-07 is complete.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What does IPS do?
2. What does a direct cockpit administrator signal?
3. What did ADR-07 decide?

sections.title: Session 7.6 — Cloud Applications and Their Security Models

blocks.text: Session 7.6 — Cloud Applications and Their Security Models

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Recognise that each cloud application has its own model. Apply one governance method across them. Explain cross-system SoD.
Role-based permissions with target populations (whose records a role can see)
Who can change pay, bank or termination data, and for whom?
Users in groups that grant capabilities
Who can create suppliers and approve purchases?
Role collections assigned to users or groups
Who administers the subaccount and integrations?
Who holds SYSTEM and administration privileges?

blocks.text: The governance method stays the same everywhere: owned roles, least privilege, SoD, a governed request path, reviews and logging. What changes is the vocabulary. Risk can also cross systems: one person can do half of a process in a cloud application and the other half in SAP.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE Suppliers created in Ariba flow to CEP business partners through Cloud Integration every 30 minutes (JML-11). A person who creates a supplier in Ariba and can run payments in CEP holds a cross-system version of SOD-001 that CORVANE_RS cannot see. Ariba is proposed for the FY2027 controls scope. For the database, DEF-004 found the HANA SYSTEM user used for routine administration on 22 days (group GR-F).
PM LENS Different subcontractors, different contracts, one project standard. You do not let each vendor decide its own acceptance criteria.
TRY IT 7.6 Describe how you would detect the Ariba-to-CEP supplier conflict before Ariba is in GRC.

blocks.text: Check yourself
1. What is a target population in SuccessFactors?
2. What stays the same across applications?
3. Why can CORVANE_RS not see the Ariba conflict?

sections.title: Session 7.7 — Governance Across SAP and Cloud: the IAG Decision

blocks.text: Session 7.7 — Governance Across SAP and Cloud: the IAG Decision

rows: LEARNING OUTCOMES Explain the choice between GRC on premise and IAG. Read ADR-01 as a lead decision. Plan the governance roadmap.

blocks.text: SAP Cloud Identity Access Governance (IAG) is SAP's cloud service for access analysis, requests, privileged access and certification, aimed especially at cloud applications. GRC Access Control 12.0 is the on-premise suite. Choosing between them, or running both for a while, is an architecture decision with cost, skills and audit consequences, so the lead records it with options and consequences.

rows: IN THE CORVANE CASE ADR-01 (14 April 2026): stay on GRC 12.0 for SAP, assess IAG for cloud applications in FY2027. The consequence, recorded in the decision, is two governance views for cloud applications until then. S03 lists IAG as IDS-08, not deployed.
PM LENS An architecture decision record is a change request for the design itself: what was decided, what else was considered, and what it costs later.
TRY IT 7.7 Write the three criteria you would use in FY2027 to decide whether IAG replaces or complements GRC 12.0 at Corvane.
