sections.title: Session 7 — W06 SoD & Sensitive Access Rule Matrix

blocks.text: Session 7 — W06 SoD & Sensitive Access Rule Matrix
7.1 Purpose

An SoD risk in W04, such as "a user can create a vendor and pay it", cannot be tested until it is translated into SAP terms: which transactions and authorisation objects make up each side of the conflict. W06 does that translation. It defines every conflicting function pair and every sensitive (critical) access item in technical terms, so the access analysis in Part 3 can run them against the user population and return exact results.

Where the client uses SAP GRC Access Control, W06 mirrors the active ruleset (ARA). Where it does not, W06 is the manual ruleset the consultant will run against SUIM or table extracts (AGR_USERS, AGR_1251, USR02).
7.2 Workbook structure

rows: One row per business function (e.g. Vendor Master Maintenance) with its transactions
Authorisation objects, fields and values that make each transaction executable (e.g. F_LFA1_BUK ACTVT 01/02)
One row per conflicting function pair, linked to RISK-ID
Critical access that is risky on its own (SAP_ALL, SE16N edit, SCC4, SE06, PFCG in PRD, debug-change)
Approved mitigating controls for accepted conflicts, linked to CTRL-ID
Version, source (GRC ARA export or manual), approval date

blocks.text: 7.3 Data fields — SoD_Rules tab

rows: Must exist in W04, category SoD
Whether the conflict applies within the same company code / plant
Business owner who approved the rule

blocks.text: 7.4 Data fields — Sensitive_Access tab

rows: Transaction, profile or auth object value
S_TABU_DIS ACTVT 02 with SE16N; SAP_ALL; S_DEVELOP ACTVT 02 (debug-change)
Direct table changes bypass application controls
Firefighter IDs only; none in PRD dialog users

blocks.text: 7.5 Worked example — ABC Manufacturing
7.6 How W06 is populated
Step 1 — Obtain the client ruleset. Export the GRC ARA ruleset (functions, actions, permissions, risks) or the client's documented SoD matrix. If neither exists, start from the TIB baseline ruleset.
Step 2 — Map every W04 SoD risk to at least one rule, and every rule back to a W04 risk. Rules with no risk are noise; risks with no rule are untestable.
Step 3 — Add permission-level detail (authorisation object, field, value) so that users with a transaction but no real ability to act are not reported as conflicts.
Step 4 — Include custom transactions (Z-codes) that replicate standard functions. These are the most common gap in client rulesets.
Step 5 — Record approved mitigations and the sensitive-access list, then have the rule owner approve the version.
7.7 Common errors
Transaction-only rules that report thousands of false positives.
Missing custom Z-transactions and Fiori app equivalents.
Accepting a "mitigation" that is not a real, tested control in W05.
Treating sensitive access as SoD; SAP_ALL is a risk on its own, without a second function.

rows: W06 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every SoD risk in W04 maps to at least one SOD-ID, and every rule maps to a risk. Rules carry permission-level detail and include custom transactions. Sensitive access items are listed with allowed holders. Mitigations point to real CTRL-IDs; the ruleset version is approved.

sections.title: Session 8 — W07 Control & Evidence Owner Matrix

blocks.text: Session 8 — W07 Control & Evidence Owner Matrix
8.1 Purpose

W07 records, for every control in the RCM, who is accountable for it, who performs it day to day, who can provide the evidence and who the backup is. These are often different people. The Head of IT Security may own the access review control, a GRC administrator may run the review campaign, and a Basis analyst may be the only person who can extract the user listing. If the testing team does not know who provides each piece of evidence, the PBC process stalls.
In the Lab 1 draft this matrix was keyed by control area. In the full foundation it is keyed by CTRL-ID, so it lines up one-to-one with the RCM.
8.2 Data fields

rows: Accountable for the risk (lookup from W04)
Person who executes it day to day
Person or team who can produce the evidence
Person who will demonstrate the control in TOD

blocks.text: 8.3 Worked example — ABC Manufacturing

rows: HR Operations (leavers list); Basis (SU01 change docs)
Basis (STMS import history); ITSM admin (change tickets)
SAP functional support (OMR6 config, change log)

blocks.text: 8.4 How W07 is populated

Start from the RCM, one row per CTRL-ID. Pre-fill the control owner from W05, then confirm each owner in a short meeting. For each control ask two separate questions: who makes sure this happens, and who can give us the evidence that it happened? Record the walkthrough contact for the design test. Mark anything unresolved as Outstanding with a follow-up; never record it as a control failure.

rows: W07 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every in-scope CTRL-ID has a row. Control owner and evidence owner are identified or marked Outstanding. Walkthrough contacts are known for every key control. Outstanding owners are escalated in the W14 dependency list.

sections.title: Session 9 — W08 PBC / Evidence Request Register

blocks.text: Session 9 — W08 PBC / Evidence Request Register
9.1 Purpose

"PBC" means Provided By Client. W08 lists every piece of evidence requested, from whom, for which period, and for which control and test. Every request must answer a future testing question. If a request cannot be traced to a CTRL-ID and a planned test, it should not be made: unnecessary requests waste the client's time and damage the engagement relationship.
9.2 Two kinds of request

Population requests — complete lists from which samples will be drawn (all users created in the period, all transports imported to PRD, all Firefighter sessions, all leavers from HR). These are also IPE and require completeness and accuracy checks in W09.

Sample evidence requests — the supporting documents for the specific items selected in W12 (the approval ticket for transport ECDK900123, the review sign-off for Firefighter session FF-0412). These are raised after sampling, as a second wave.
9.3 Data fields

rows: Exactly what is needed, including format and fields
e.g. SM20/STMS import history PRD, all imports 01-Jan to 30-Sep, CSV with request no., date, user
Requested / Partially received / Received / Rejected – incomplete / Closed

blocks.text: 9.4 Worked example — ABC Manufacturing

rows: All SAP users in ECP/300 (USR02 extract: user, type, valid from/to, lock status, last logon)
HR leavers report for 01-Jan to 30-Sep with termination dates
GRC EAM Firefighter log report, all sessions in period
STMS import history to ECP, all transports in period
SCC4 and SE06 settings for ECP with change logs
OMR6 tolerance configuration and table change log (CDHDR/CDPOS or DBTABLOG)
Change tickets and test sign-off for 25 sampled transports (list from SMP-003)

blocks.text: 9.5 How W08 is populated
Step 1 — Generate wave 1 and 2 requests from the RCM. For each in-scope key control, read the Expected evidence and Test approach columns and write the population and configuration requests needed.
Step 2 — Consolidate. One USR02 extract serves several access controls; raise it once and list all CTRL-IDs.
Step 3 — Make each request precise: system, client, period, fields, format. Vague requests produce unusable evidence.
Step 4 — Issue, then track daily during fieldwork. Update Status and add EV-IDs as items arrive and are indexed in W09.
Step 5 — Raise wave 3 sample requests only after W12 sampling is complete.

rows: W08 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every request traces to at least one CTRL-ID (and TEST-ID once W10 exists). Every request states system, period and required fields. Population requests are flagged for IPE checks. Outstanding requests are visible with owner and due date.

sections.title: Session 10 — W09 Evidence Index & IPE Log

blocks.text: Session 10 — W09 Evidence Index & IPE Log
10.1 Purpose

W09 is the filing system. Every item received is given an EV-ID, its source and extraction details are recorded, the original is preserved untouched, and population-type evidence is checked for completeness and accuracy before any sample is drawn from it. That last step is the IPE (Information Produced by the Entity) check. If a population is incomplete, every sample from it is unreliable, and so is every conclusion.
10.2 Data fields — Evidence_Index tab

rows: t-code / report / table / GRC report / ITSM export / manual document
Is it a population or report relied on

blocks.text: 10.3 The IPE check
For each population, the IPE_Log tab records how completeness (nothing is missing) and accuracy (the data is correct) were established. Typical procedures are:
Observe or evidence the extraction. The tester watches the report being run, or receives a screenshot showing the selection parameters (system, client, date range, no restrictive filters).
Reconcile record counts to an independent source, for example the user count in USR02 against SUIM, or the import count in STMS against the transport log.
Test parameters and logic for custom reports: confirm the selection logic does not exclude records (such as locked users or a company code).
Trace a few records both ways: from the system to the file (completeness) and from the file to the system (accuracy).

rows: Count agreed to SUIM RSUSR002 total; parameters screenshot shows no filters
Count agreed to STMS import queue history; date range verified
Count reconciled to HR headcount movement report

W09 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every received item has an EV-ID, standard filename and preserved original. Every population has an IPE check recorded. No sample is drawn from a population with IPE result other than Pass. W08 status is updated with EV-IDs.

sections.title: Session 11 — W10 Test Plan / Testing Program

blocks.text: Session 11 — W10 Test Plan / Testing Program
11.1 Purpose

W10 converts the RCM into a schedule of tests. For every in-scope key control it creates two rows: a test of design (TOD) and a test of operating effectiveness (TOE). Each row states the test attributes, the procedure, the population, the sample size, the period, the tester, the reviewer and the planned dates. This is where the scope of work becomes a plan the team can execute and a manager can track.
11.2 Design versus operating effectiveness

rows: If performed as described, would this control address the risk?
Did the control actually operate throughout the period?
Walkthrough of one instance: inquiry plus observation or inspection
Inspection or reperformance of a sample across the period
Size driven by frequency and risk (11.4)
Interim and/or roll-forward to period end
Design deficiency; TOE is not performed

blocks.text: 11.3 Data fields

rows: One TOD and one TOE per key control
ITGC-APD / PC / CO / ITAC / IPE / BPC
The specific conditions each sample item must meet
Each attribute traceable to control description
Inquiry / Observation / Inspection / Reperformance with steps
Whether dependent ITGCs must be effective
Not started / In progress / Ready for review / Reviewed / Closed

blocks.text: 11.4 Typical sample size guide
The table below reflects common practice for SOX testing. Always apply the methodology of the engagement firm or the external auditor where one is specified.

rows: 1 per configuration, provided dependent ITGCs are effective (baseline / benchmarking)

blocks.text: 11.5 Worked example — test attributes

rows: Attributes (each sample item must meet all)

A: Leaver appears in the HR leavers report   B: SAP user locked or end-dated (SU01 change history)   C: Lock date within two business days of termination date   D: No logon after termination date (USR02 last logon / SM20)

A: Change ticket exists and is approved before import   B: Evidence of testing in QAS with sign-off   C: Import to PRD performed by a user other than the developer   D: Transport contents agree to the approved change

blocks.text: 11.6 How W10 is populated

Filter the RCM for SOX in scope = Y. For each control create the TOD and TOE rows. Derive the attributes directly from the five-part control description; each attribute tests one part of it. Set the sample size from the frequency. Mark ITGC reliance for ITAC, IPE and ITDM controls. Assign testers and reviewers, then schedule ITGC tests first, because their results determine how much reliance can be placed on automated controls.

rows: CORE INSIGHT — SCHEDULE ITGCs FIRST Testing the three-way match before Program Change testing is complete means the ITAC result may have to be reopened. Plan the access and change ITGCs in the first fieldwork window and the ITACs after them.

W10 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every SOX in-scope key control has a TOD and a TOE row. Every row has attributes derived from the control description. Sample sizes follow the guide or a justified deviation. ITGC tests are scheduled before dependent ITAC/IPE tests.

blocks.text: Session 12 — W11 Test Workpapers
12.1 Purpose

A workpaper is the record of what the tester actually did. It must allow an experienced reviewer who was not involved to understand the test, reperform it and reach the same conclusion. W11 is a set of templates, one per control area, all sharing the same structure so that every test across the project reads the same way.
12.2 Standard workpaper structure

rows: TEST-ID, CTRL-ID, RISK-ID(s), control description, SYS-ID, period, tester, reviewer, dates
The question the test answers, in one sentence
EV-ID, record count, IPE-ID and result
SMP-ID from W12 and selection method
Numbered steps actually performed, including t-codes and tables used
One row per sample item, one column per attribute, with tick / exception and EV-ID reference
Description, root cause from inquiry, and whether it is a deviation or a false positive
Effective / Exception noted / Ineffective, with rationale

blocks.text: 12.3 Templates by control area
Parts 3A and 3B of this manual take each template in turn, with SAP navigation and worked tests. The set is:

rows: GRC ARM requests, SU01 change documents, USR02
HR leavers report, USR02 lock/validity, last logon
GRC UAR campaign, review sign-offs, removal evidence
SUIM by profile (SAP_ALL, SAP_NEW), USR02 user types, DDIC/SAP* status
GRC EAM logs, request/approval, controller review
GRC ARA user-level results, W06 ruleset, mitigation assignment
STMS import history, E070/E071, ITSM change tickets
SM20 security audit log, S_DEVELOP holders
Backup logs, restore test evidence (often SOC 1 for hosted)
SPRO paths (OMR6, OB52, credit control), table change logs
Report logic, parameters, completeness and accuracy procedures

W11 IS COMPLETE WHEN Each test has a completed workpaper in the standard structure. Every attribute result references an EV-ID. Exceptions are explained with root cause. The reviewer has signed off before the result is entered in W10.

blocks.text: Session 13 — W12 Sample Selection Log
13.1 Purpose

W12 records exactly which items were chosen from which population, by what method, and why. It allows a reviewer to confirm the sample was unbiased and covered the whole period, and it drives the wave 3 PBC requests for supporting evidence.
13.2 Data fields

rows: Random (seeded) / Systematic / Haphazard / Targeted (risk-based) / All items
User IDs, transport numbers, FF session IDs

blocks.text: 13.3 Worked example

For C-ITGC-PC-001-TOE, the population EV-019 contains 312 transports imported to ECP between 01-Jan and 30-Sep (IPE-002 Pass). The event-driven guide gives a sample of 25. The tester uses Excel RAND with seed 4471, checks that every month is represented, adds two targeted items (emergency transports imported outside the change window), lists the 27 transport numbers on the Items tab and raises PBC-040 for the change tickets and test sign-offs.

rows: W12 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every TOE has a sample logged with method and parameters. The sample covers the whole period. Targeted additions are explained. Wave 3 PBC requests are raised and cross-referenced.

blocks.text: Session 14 — W13 Deficiency & Remediation Log
14.1 Purpose

W13 records every test exception that is confirmed as a deficiency, evaluates its severity, links it back through the thread to the risk and process affected, and tracks remediation and retesting. An exception is not automatically a deficiency: it may be a false positive (for example, a "conflict" that the permission-level analysis shows cannot actually be executed) or it may be within the tolerated deviation rate for the sample.
14.2 Severity levels

rows: The control does not allow management or employees to prevent or detect misstatements on a timely basis.
Less severe than a material weakness, yet important enough to merit the attention of those responsible for oversight (audit committee).
A reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.

blocks.text: Severity is judged on the magnitude of the potential misstatement and the likelihood it occurs, taking into account compensating controls. For ITGC deficiencies, the evaluation also considers which dependent ITAC, IPE and ITDM controls are affected (read from the W05 ITGC_Dependency tab).
14.3 Data fields

rows: Number of failed items out of sample
Remediated control must operate long enough to be tested
Open / Remediation in progress / Retest / Closed

blocks.text: 14.4 Worked example

DEF-004 — C-ITGC-AC-002-TOE found that 3 of 25 sampled leavers were locked between 6 and 14 business days after termination, and one (user JSMITH) logged on after the termination date. Condition: late removal. Criteria: removal within two business days. Cause: the HR leavers report is sent weekly, not daily. Effect: leavers retain the ability to post transactions. Dependent controls affected: C-ITGC-AC-003 is the compensating control (quarterly review) and was effective; the post-termination logon was investigated through SM20 and showed display-only activity. Severity: control deficiency. Remediation: daily HR feed into GRC with automatic lock; retest after 60 days of operation.

rows: W13 IS COMPLETE WHEN Every confirmed exception has a DEF-ID traced to test, control, risk and process. Severity is evaluated, including impact on dependent controls and compensating controls. Management response, owner and due date are recorded. Retest is planned for every remediated deficiency.

sections.title: Session 15 — W14 Scoping Workpaper & Coverage Dashboard

blocks.text: Session 15 — W14 Scoping Workpaper & Coverage Dashboard
15.1 Purpose

W14 is the master record and the reviewer's first stop. During scoping it summarises what is in scope, what is confirmed and what is outstanding (the role played by 06_Lab1_Scoping_Workpaper in the draft). As the project progresses it becomes the coverage dashboard: it proves that every risk has a control, every key control has been tested, and every deficiency has been evaluated.
15.2 Workbook structure

rows: Client, period, materiality basis, systems and processes in scope (lookups from W01 and W03)
Three-column view separating validated facts, unconfirmed items and outstanding requests
Access gaps, missing owners, missing evidence, IPE failures, each with owner and date
One row per SOX-relevant risk: mapped key controls, TOD result, TOE result, deficiencies, residual status
For each ITAC/IPE/ITDM control: dependent ITGCs and their results, and whether reliance is supported
Counts by status: PBC requests, tests, workpapers reviewed, deficiencies open
Scoping stage: "No conclusion at scoping stage." Final stage: overall assessment by process and control category

blocks.text: 15.3 Coverage checks (formulas)

rows: Every SOX-relevant RISK-ID has ≥ 1 key CTRL-ID in Risk_Control_Map
Every key CTRL-ID has a TOD and a TOE row in W10
Every TEST-ID has a population EV-ID with IPE = Pass
Every TOE has an SMP-ID covering the full period
Every TEST-ID has a reviewed result
Every Ineffective or Exception-noted test has a DEF-ID or a documented false-positive rationale
Every ITAC/IPE/ITDM shows all dependent ITGCs Effective, or has additional procedures recorded

blocks.text: 15.4 Worked example — Coverage_Matrix extract

rows: CORE INSIGHT — W14 TELLS THE STORY A partner or audit committee member should be able to open W14 and, without opening any other workbook, see what was in scope, what was tested, what failed and what remains open. Every number on it is a formula over W01–W13, never a typed figure.

W14 IS COMPLETE WHEN Scoping stage: in-scope items, known/unconfirmed/outstanding and dependencies are complete, and the conclusion reads "No conclusion at scoping stage". Testing stage: every coverage check passes or the gap is explained. All figures are formulas linked to the source workbooks.

sections.title: Session 16 — The Population Sequence and Checkpoints

blocks.text: Session 16 — The Population Sequence and Checkpoints
16.1 Why order matters

Each workbook depends on keys created in earlier ones. Populating out of order produces broken links, duplicate requests and tests against unconfirmed scope. The sequence below is the order a TIB engagement follows, with a checkpoint (gate) that must be passed before the next stage starts.
16.2 The sequence

rows: Landscape diagram, system inventory, System > Status, SCC4, SM51, SM59, WE20, STMS routes
G1: all financially relevant systems and interfaces listed and validated or flagged
Significant accounts/FSLIs, process narratives, transaction usage
G2: every significant account maps to a process; technical areas added
Risk library, walkthrough interviews, prior audit issues, W01–W03 gaps
G3: every BP-ID has risks; SOX risks flagged; owners agreed
Client RCM, policies, GRC ruleset, configuration
G4: every SOX risk has a key control; ITGC dependencies recorded; ruleset approved
G5: owners confirmed or escalated as dependencies
G6: populations received and IPE Pass
G7: TOD/TOE rows for all key controls; ITGCs scheduled first
Test results, compensating controls, management responses
G9: all coverage checks pass; deficiencies evaluated; conclusion signed

blocks.text: 16.3 Scoping deliverable versus testing deliverable

Stages 1 to 5, plus wave 1 and 2 PBC requests, make up the scope of work (the deliverable from the Lab 1 scoping exercise). At the end of stage 5, W14 is issued in its scoping form with the conclusion "No conclusion at scoping stage". Stages 6 to 9 are the testing phase, which the scope of work plans and controls. The scope of work is therefore not a separate document; it is the state of W01–W08 and W14 at gate G5.
16.4 Iteration

The sequence is not strictly one-way. A walkthrough in stage 3 often reveals an interface missing from W02, or a test in stage 8 shows a control works differently from its RCM description. When this happens, update the source workbook, keep the existing keys, and let the links flow forward. Never patch a downstream workbook to cover an upstream gap.

rows: FINAL TRACEABILITY TEST Pick any row in W13 or W14. A trainee should be able to follow it back: DEF → TEST → SMP → EV → PBC → OWNER → CTRL → RISK → BP → INT → SYS, and name the server, client and process owner it came from. If any link breaks, the foundation is not complete.

blocks.text: End of Part 2

Parts 1 and 2 together define the full Foundation Workbook Set and the order in which it is built. Parts 3A and 3B take each W11 workpaper template in turn (access, emergency access, SoD, change, operations, ITAC configuration and IPE) and walks through the SAP navigation, test steps and worked results for ABC Manufacturing. Part 4 covers deficiency evaluation in depth and the end-to-end trace exercise.

Length: 6 to 16 minutes, as listed. One idea per video.

Corvane Weekly Activity Plan | Corvane Energy Group
Purpose

Converts the Corvane Story into discrete activities grouped by week for the 38 calendar weeks from 12 January to 30 September 2026. Each activity has an owner, supporters, client stakeholders, the workbook where it is recorded and the output that shows it is done. Week_Summary gives the focus and gate of each week; Pod_Activity shows how work moves between the pods.
How to use this workbook
1. Filter Weekly_Plan by Week to see what the team does that week, or by Owner or Pod to follow one person or pod across the project.
2. Read Week_Summary for the phase, gate and focus of each week.
3. Read Pod_Activity to see when each pod is busy and when it is free to help another.
4. To reuse on a new project, change the start date in Setup, replace the activities and re-read Checks.
Colour legend
Yellow cells with blue text = input. Grey cells = formulas (do not overwrite). Weekly_Plan holds one discrete activity per row, grouped by project week; Week_Summary, Team and Pod_Activity read it.
Completion gate
Every week has at least one discrete activity with an owner and an output.
Gates G1 to G9 each fall in a stated week.
Every owner is a member of the team.
Manual reference
The Corvane Story, chapters 1 to 12; Controls Lead Playbook sections 2, 3 and 5.

blocks.text: TIB SYSTEMS LLC  |  SAP Controls Project Foundation Workbook Set
W01 — Landscape & System Inventory | PRACTICE CASE: CORVANE LITE
Purpose

Records every SAP system, client and supporting component that holds financial data or processes business transactions, and states whether each is in scope and whether it has actually been validated. W01 is the root of the golden thread: every other workbook points back to a SYS-ID.
How to use this workbook
1. Enter the client-provided landscape in System_Inventory with Validation status = Documented only.
2. Validate directly (System > Status, SCC4, SM51, DB02). Upgrade the status to Validated and add the evidence ref.
3. Record application servers and hosts in Server_Detail, and the STMS route in Transport_Routes.
4. Decide scope and record a rationale for every exclusion.
5. Log every unresolved question in Open_Items. Finish by reading the Checks tab.
Colour legend

Yellow cells with blue text = input. Grey cells = formulas (do not overwrite). This is a PRACTICE copy: the registers are empty. Enter the facts from the Practice Case Brief, then read the Checks tab.
Completion gate
Every known component is listed with SID, client and environment.
Every row has In scope = Y/N with a rationale for N.
Every Validated row has an evidence reference; every other row has an open question.
The PRD transport route is recorded.
Manual reference
Part 1, Session 2 (W01).

blocks.text: 2. The Case in One Page

Corvane Energy Group runs one production S/4HANA system for all four company codes. The project lead has asked you to record a small slice of the foundation: the vendor payment and treasury processes and the access control that protects them. The slice has six systems, two bank interfaces, four processes (one of them technical), two financial statement accounts, five risks and five controls. The process owners are the Head of AP, the Treasury Manager and the IT Security Manager.

Evidence is the leavers report annotated with lock dates and the SU01 change history (evidence).

The GRC administrator (who) runs access risk analysis at every provisioning request and monthly for all users against the approved ruleset (what), so conflicts are removed or assigned an approved, tested mitigating control (when and how, in GRC ARA). The AP Analyst (who) verifies every vendor bank-detail change by calling the vendor on an independently sourced number before the change is saved (what) for every change (when) using the call-back procedure and log (how). Evidence is the call-back log with approver (evidence).

Treasury (who) confirms for every payment run that the file hash received by the bank equals the F110 file, restricts write access to the file directory, and reconciles the bank confirmation total to the F110 total (what) at every payment run (when) using the CPI file-hash alert and the bank confirmation (how). The Treasury Analyst (who) confirms that every bank statement expected for the day was loaded in FF_5 and chases any missing statement (what) every day (when) using the statement load log and the bank list (how). Evidence is the daily load checklist (evidence).

Open the answer-key workbooks and compare each of your registers. Note every difference and say whether it matters
Find the 18 seeded errors in the Find_the_Errors folder and record them in Error_Log_Template.xlsx

blocks.text: Task 7: Find the errors

Six Corvane workbooks (X01 to X06) have had errors seeded into them. Fifteen of the errors make a check show a message; three are silent and can only be found by reading the data and thinking about whether it makes sense. For each error, log the workbook, tab, key, what is wrong, the message shown (if any), how you found it, and the fix.

rows: One row claims more than its evidence shows; one key is not what it should be
Look at statements, keys and owners; one error is invisible to the checks
A short description, a missing dependency, a broken link, and one silent error
A file name and a result in the evidence index
Closure, group rating and one silent error

blocks.text: Marking

rows: Each error found, logged with the right key and a fix

A WORD ON THE SILENT ERRORS Checks measure completeness, not correctness. A workbook can read OK on every row and still carry a wrong owner, a wrong frequency or a wrong group. Reading for sense is part of the job, not an extra.

README and navigation guide  |  Training package for a new controls lead  |  Version 0.1  |  October 2026

Corvane Energy Group is a fictitious integrated oil and gas company. All people, figures and events are invented and built to be internally consistent across the 14 workbooks, the story and the playbook.
© TIB Systems LLC. Atlanta, GA | Hyderabad, India | RAK, UAE. For training use.
1. What This Package Is

A complete, worked example of a SOX-focused SAP controls project, from the landscape to the conclusion, for an oil and gas company running S/4HANA across four company codes. It contains the 14 foundation workbooks filled in end to end, the story of how the project was run, a playbook for leading the team and the stakeholders, and the reference manuals. The headline result: 30 deficiencies were logged in the baseline cycle; 21 were closed after a successful retest and 9 remain open, a 70 percent reduction. Both significant-deficiency groups were closed and there is no material weakness.
Use it to train a new controls lead who is about to run a similar project with a team of 15 and a set of senior stakeholders.

blocks.text: 4. How the Workbooks Connect

Each workbook has a unique key and the next workbook refers to it. The thread is: system, interface, process, risk, control, owner, evidence request, evidence item, test, sample, deficiency, conclusion. The keys are pasted as values into the Ref_ tabs of the next workbook (see Deployment Guide section 4), so every file stands alone. In this package every Ref_ tab matches its source workbook exactly.

rows: 61 (11 supported, 49 supported with additional procedures, 1 not relied on)

blocks.text: 6. Status of the Files

All 14 workbooks were recalculated and checked: every Checks tab reads ALL CHECKS PASS, there are no formula errors, and the Ref_ tabs agree with their source workbooks (risks, controls, tests, evidence, requests, deficiencies, processes and systems). No placeholder text from the blank templates remains in the Corvane files.
Points to know

The nine open deficiencies are deliberate. They need further operating cycles or an event (an emergency change) before a retest is meaningful. Their owners and due dates (27 November to 18 December 2026) are in W13, and the planned retests are in W10.
Dates and counts depend on the as-of date of 30 September 2026. Some formulas use today's date (days overdue), so these figures change as time passes.

The six worked workpapers in W11 (leavers, transports, Firefighter sessions, vendor call-backs, interface monitoring and the three-way match) carry real sample items from W12; other tests are logged in the W11 register with their results and deficiency links.
Everything is fictitious. Names of people, systems, figures and companies are invented for training. Do not rely on any figure as a benchmark.
Method versus case. The blank templates and manuals (folder 06) are generic. The Corvane files are one worked example, not a standard.
7. How to Reuse the Package
Run a training lab: give trainees the blank templates and the Corvane story and ask them to rebuild W01 to W05 from the case facts, then compare to the completed files.
Run the trace exercise: pick any deficiency in W13 and trace it back through W11, W10, W09, W08, W05, W04 and W01.
Start a real engagement: copy Blank_Workbook_Templates into a new engagement folder and follow the Deployment Guide.
Brief a new lead: read the Story and Playbook, then work through the first 30, 60 and 90 days plan.

blocks.text: 4.1 Points to know
The S01 role register is a sample. Its unused share (43 percent) is higher than the catalogue figure (37 percent) because the sample includes every legacy role. Quote the catalogue figure.
The access review control passed its test (C-ITGC-AC-003-TOE). The rubber-stamping found in S04 is a quality issue a lead should act on, not a deficiency.
Identity and cloud systems take IDS-IDs, not SYS-IDs. None is in the FY2026 controls scope; Ariba is proposed for FY2027.
Findings in the extension are new observations. Where an observation matches an existing deficiency (for example DEF-001, DEF-005 or DEF-010), the extension links to it rather than logging a new one.
